surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Panthers edge the Kings
paras: Alex Laferriere opened the scoring for the Kings late in the first, and that was all they would get. Seth Jones tied it 1-1 for Florida early in the second, and Garnet Hathaway and Joel Edmundson dropped the gloves midway through the period. Matthew Tkachuk put the Panthers ahead for good midway through the third.

The Panthers had a bit more of the good stuff, outshooting the Kings 30-20 (20-10 at 5-on-5). Jacob Markström made 19 saves for the Cats, and Darcy Kuemper stopped 28 of 30 at the other end. By our Swing measure, Erik Haula had the best night of anyone, even in a loss.

Neither power play scored: the Panthers killed all five Kings power plays, and the Kings killed all six of Florida’s. The Panthers killed off a two-man advantage that lasted less than two minutes late in the first. The Panthers moved to 2-0-2 and climbed into first in the Atlantic, while the Kings fell to 0-2-1, seventh in the Pacific.

items.text: Matthew Tkachuk passed Róbert Švehla for a tie for tenth on the Panthers’ all-time scoring list, with 291 points.
The Kings are winless in three (0-2-1).
The Panthers are 2-0-2, still without a regulation loss.
The Kings lost their home opener, and the Panthers have now beaten them four straight times, going back to the 2024-25 season.
